1.name: Record relationship
1.description: A relationship of a defined type between two records in the database, may include a time range over which the relationship is valid, and notes about the relationship

2.name: Web bookmark (site or page)
2.description: A web site URL, typically a specific page (may be the home page of a website or specific pages or documents of interest)

3.name: Notes
3.description: A simple record type for taking notes

4.name: Organisation
4.description: Organisations (companies, universities, granting bodies, museums, libraries etc.)

5.name: Digital media (image, video, PDF etc.)
5.description: Any sort of digital files - typically media (image, sound, video), but can also include word processing, presentation or data files - uploaded to the database or referenced at an external URL. Use this where the media file is likely to be referenced by multiple records or you wish to record metadata about the file.

6.name: Aggregation/Collection
6.description: A record which describes a static or dynamic collection of records and their filtering and layout, or acts as a root to which other records point, or both

7.name: Blog post (for website)
7.description: Blog post used to construct blogs, the text of the post is stored in the WYSIWYG text field, the blog is implemented as a component on the CMS website

8.name: Interpretive annotation
8.description: Metadata about a date, spatial extent or other interpretation of information

9.name: Email
9.description: An email including content and metadata, often derived from an email forwarded or ccd to the database's linked IMAP server from a user's account

10.name: Person
10.description: A record for a Person, for routine use eg. for authors, painters, historical figures.

11.name: Map image file (tiled)
11.description: MAP DATA SOURCE: A tiled image set for display as a layer on e.g. a Google map

12.name: Place
12.description: A simplified record for a Place, for routine use eg. for site location, place of birth, place of publication. Use Place (detailed) where more information is needed.

24.name: Heurist Map Document
24.description: A record describing the construction of a map from map layers in the current database. Includes generic settings for the map document and pointers to map layer records, theme groupings and other relevant information

25.name: Heurist Map Layer
25.description: A layer to appear in a map. Specifies data source, symbology, labelling and behaviours

27.name: Map file data source
27.description: MAP FILE DATA SOURCE: Spatial data supplied as a KML, CSV, TST or GeoJSON file, archive, URL or text snippet, generally for use as a map layer.

28.name: Map image file (non-tiled)
28.description: MAP DATA SOURCE: A single (non-tiled) map image file in JPG, TIF, GeoTIF, PNG etc., generally for use as a map layer

29.name: Query Data Source
29.description:
A reusable definition of a Heurist query and selected record fields for map source, timeline, tabular display, publication or export.
Query Data Source can be used as the source of a map layer - the objects retrieved by the query contribute their spatial and/or temporal data, plus name, icon and potentially other attributes, to the content of the layer

44.name: Shapefile
44.description: MAP DATA SOURCE: Shapefile file, generally for use as a map layer

48.name: Life event
48.description: A dated and/or spatially located fact about a person eg. birth, death, burial. Can also be applied to organisations, structures etc.

51.name: CMS_Home
51.description: The root of a Heurist-constructed CMS website menu, includes general description of the website

52.name: CMS Menu-Page
52.description: A menu within the CMS website. A menu can point to one or more other menus and/or to one or more menu leaves which are links to CMS pages (static html which may embed dynamic elements)..

53.name: Simple table (CSV, TSV, DBF)
53.description: MAP DATA SOURCE: a file with a simple row/column structure, for use as a map layer. Record needs to specify the meanings of the columns

54.name: Event - contemporary
54.description: Present day events such as lectures, performances, exhibitions, rallies etc., typically with precise location and date/time(s)

55.name: Event - historical
55.description: Historical events such as wars or other significant occurances

56.name: Eventlet
56.description: An event-based assertion, generally about a point on a lifeline of a person or object, such as birth, marriage, loans of an item or destruction of a building

57.name: Funding Program
57.description: Grant or funding program - use record for each individual grant program within a larger funding organisation, then link these to the organisation record

58.name: Grant
58.description: Research or other grant, specific to a project (use grant progrqam and organisation to define a series of grants in a program, such as ARC Linkage grants)

60.name: Group or association
60.description: An informally constituted but identifiable group of people, or a formally constituted association

61.name: Educational institution
61.description: An educational institution - school, college, TAFE, community college, university etc.

62.name: Interview
62.description: An interview, generally of a person, may include audio, video and/or transcription(s)

63.name: Translation
63.description: A translation of a text into a given language. Will typically be connected as a child record of a record containing the original text.

64.name: Jurisdiction
64.description: A nation state or branch of government

65.name: Place role instance
65.description: The role or function of a place for a specified period of time

66.name: Structure
66.description: A building or other human-constructed structure

67.name: Archival record
67.description: An item of any type that is in an archival collection

68.name: Archival record series
68.description: The record series to which an archival item is normally assigned

69.name: Book chapter
69.description: A chapter or section of a book, generally a multi-author edited book

70.name: Book
70.description: A book may be authored or edited or both, it may be part of a series and normally has a publisher. If it is a proceedings volume it can be linked to the conference record

71.name: Publication series
71.description: A publication series defining a group of related works from a publisher

72.name: Conference
72.description: Use this type for the conference itself rather than the proceedings (which should be entered as a book or journal volume and connected to the conference in the Conference Proceedings field)

73.name: Journal article
73.description: An article published in a journal

74.name: Journal volume
74.description: A specific issue (volume/part) of a journal

75.name: Journal
75.description: A serial publication in the form of a journal

76.name: Report
76.description: Generally an unpublished commissioned work, which investigates or documents a specific question or issue

77.name: Thesis
77.description: A thesis or dissertation submitted in support of candidature for an academic degree

78.name: Magazine article
78.description: An article published in a magazine

79.name: Magazine volume
79.description: A specific issue (volume/part) of a magazine

80.name: Magazine
80.description: A serial publication in the form of a magazine

81.name: Newspaper article
81.description: An article published in a newspaper

82.name: Newspaper volume
82.description: A specific issue (volume/part) of a newspaper

83.name: Newspaper
83.description: A serial publication in the form of a newspaper

84.name: Artwork
84.description: BIBLIOGRAPHIC description of a painting, sketch, etching, engraving, or other artwork. Use Digital Media Item if the main aim is to store and deliver the images themselves, or to index images in a third party repository

85.name: Map
85.description: A BIBLIOGRAPHIC description of a map, plan, sketch or any other cartographic item. Use record types under spatial and mapping for actual map data (georeferenced images, KML files etc.)

86.name: Other document
86.description: A document, generally unpublished, that does not fit into one of the existing bibliographic types

87.name: Photograph
87.description: An image of any type produced by a photographic process. Use this for a BIBLIOGRAPHIC description of a photograph. Use Digital Media item to store and access photographs.

88.name: Personal communication
88.description: A source of information that is personal, such as a conversation, telephone call, fax, letter or email

89.name: Document
89.description: A document, typically represented by a PDF (or link to a PDF) or other source. Documents may be referenced relative to a source such as a newspaper, archive or private collection.

92.name: Project
92.description: The project under which the work is done

99.name: Map Layer Style
99.description: A record containing a map layer style field which can be selected to override default symbologies for Heurist map layers or for map datasets

100.name: Story element
100.description: A step in a story eg. events in a person's life history

101.name: Map Annotation
101.description: A record which annotates a position on an image or map image (typically an IIIF or tilestack image). The area annotated may be defined in lat/long or in other coordinates eg. image pixels for non-georeferenced images. IIIF images annotated with Mirador will use IIIF standards.

102.name: Bibliographic reference
102.description: A reference with page number and notes to any of the bibliographic record types

103.name: Task (Feature, Bug, Issue)
103.description: A bug report or feature requirements

104.name: Work package
104.description: A group of tasks or work items required to complete the project

107.name: CMS Menu-Action
107.description: A menu within the CMS website. A menu executes the specified action with defined parameters

108.name: Team member
108.description: A record for a Person involved in the project eg. researcher, volunteer, consultant

109.name: IIIF Annotation
109.description: A Web Annotation associated with a IIIF Canvas, Manifest, or media resource. Used to store annotations imported from IIIF manifests, created in Mirador, or edited in Heurist.

110.name: IIIF Manifest
110.description: A managed or registered IIIF Presentation Manifest. Used to store manifest metadata, the source manifest file or URL, import mode, and settings for generating IIIF output from Heurist.

111.name: IIIF Canvas
111.description: A IIIF Canvas or media target used by a managed IIIF Manifest. Stores the Canvas identity, order, label, source media, and original Canvas metadata when imported.

126.name: File Resource
126.description: File Resource. Uploaded or registered in the system
